llm.reply:
The KRAS gene product functions biochemically as a small GTPase [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. In cellular signaling networks, the active protein operates as an on-off switch that continuously stimulates downstream cellular pathways [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"].

## Enzymatic Activity

The official gene name is KRAS [5]. The protein operates as a GTPase enzyme [4]. It belongs to a broader group of small GTP-binding proteins [11: "member of the small GTPase superfamily"].

## Signaling Function

Single residue alterations produce constitutively active variants [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. These oncogenic forms act as switches that drive key downstream programs for cell survival and multiplication [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival"]. Normal regulation can involve upstream exchange factors like Son of Sevenless 1 [29: "guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"].

The KRAS gene product functions as a small GTPase that serves as a molecular switch [4][11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"][26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"]. The official gene symbol is KRAS [1]. Its full gene name is KRAS [5].

## Gene Function and Variants
Alternative splicing yields isoforms differing at the C-terminus, while single substitutions confer activating oncogenic properties [11: "Alternative splicing leads to variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"][11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. One recorded variant is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. Another documented variant is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. Another sequence alteration is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. Additionally, literature identifies the entity as Kras [6].

## Pathogenic Mechanisms and Signatures
Mutated KRAS activates TFCP2 to trigger CAF transformation into lipid-rich cells that secrete VEGFA to drive vascularization in colorectal carcinoma [28: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2) that upregulates the expression of the proadipogenic factors BMP4 and WNT5B, triggering the transformation of CAFs into lipid-rich CAFs"][28: "These lipid-rich CAFs, in turn, produce VEGFA to spur angiogenesis"]. A related variant record is NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. Another cataloged variant is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23]. Several publications explore KRAS pathogenesis across malignancies, including Role of oncogenic KRAS in the prognosis, diagnosis and treatment of colorectal cancer [2][8]. Another article is KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer [9][13]. Further literature includes Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression [14][17].

## Therapeutic Targeting and Clinical Trials
Pancreatic cancer heavily features KRAS mutations, prompting both allele-specific approaches and pan-KRAS degraders capable of targeting multiple oncogenic variants [22][29: "The Kirsten rat sarcoma virus (KRAS) oncogene is mutated in up to 90% of all pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs)"][30: "heterobifunctional small molecule that potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"]. Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer details these therapeutic challenges [18][21]. Pan-KRAS degradation has emerged as a strategy [25][27: "AMG510 was the first drug-targeting KRAS (G12C) to be approved for clinical use this year"]. Clinical investigations include Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7]. Other trials include PREMIUM, Observational Study [12]. Additional studies comprise A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16]. Clinical studies also encompass Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20]. Finally, research includes A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
